extracted.intended_audience: Duke investigators (faculty, postdocs, research staff) preparing grant proposals—especially NIH/translational and clinical research applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Institution-specific guidance for preparing competitive research grant proposals at Duke, emphasizing NIH conventions, translational framing, use of institutional cores (DTMI/DCRI), Specific Aims construction, approach/rigor, budgets, and pre-submission checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims page conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard four-paragraph structure; hypothesis-driven aims; aim independence; conceptual figure encouraged; iterate 10+ times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a clear, four-paragraph Specific Aims page that states a hypothesis, presents independent aims, and includes (where helpful) a conceptual figure. Revise the Specific Aims many times (recommendation: iterate 10+ times) to sharpen clarity and focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance and innovation framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame significance for non-specialist reviewers; cite high-impact recent papers; connect work to the NIH institute mission; present innovation as a novel application or concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the importance understandable to a general NIH reviewer, highlight recent high-impact literature, and explicitly relate the project to the target institute's priorities. Define 'innovation' in terms of novelty or novel application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach: aim-level organization and rigor
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize Approach by aim with subsections; include statistical analysis plan with power and sample size justification; address rigor and reproducibility, authentication of resources, sex as a biological variable, and alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each aim provide methods subsections, pre-specify analyses, include power calculations and sample-size rationale, describe rigorous practices (e.g., blinding, randomization where applicable), authenticate reagents/resources, address SABV, and discuss alternative approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator and environment match
rubrics_metrics.description: Productivity appropriate to career stage; cite Duke-specific resources and institutional support; provide specific letters of support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate that the PI/team record is consistent with the project's scope; highlight Duke cores, centers, and support relevant to the work; ensure letters of support speak to specific contributions and commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cores and facilities to cite
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite and leverage Duke cores (e.g., Duke Genomics Core, Light Microscopy Core, Functional Genomics Shared Resource, BERD, DCRI methodological expertise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly reference named cores and shared resources that will be used; show access and commitment from those resources to strengthen environment and feasibility claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training programs and institutional training environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite Duke training programs where relevant (e.g., MSTP, biomedical graduate programs, DCRI training programs) to demonstrate training environment or trainee support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For training grants or proposals involving trainees, document relevant institutional training programs and how they will support career development and project execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: DTMI / DCRI integration for translational projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage DTMI/DCRI clinical research infrastructure, trial design expertise, patient cohort access, and implementation science capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the project is translational or clinical, explicitly describe how DTMI/DCRI resources, cohorts, and trial expertise will be used to accelerate bench-to-bedside translation and strengthen feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community engagement and health equity framing
rubrics_metrics.description: Frame community-engaged research leveraging Duke's service to North Carolina; emphasize health equity, rural and underserved populations where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relevant, describe community partnerships, engagement strategies, and how the work addresses local/underserved populations and health equity priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translational emphasis / bench-to-bedside narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize patient-facing potential, bench-to-bedside pathways, and implementation science where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight how discoveries will move toward clinical application or implementation; cite examples of pathways, pilot data, or resources enabling translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypothesis-driven preference
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should be hypothesis-driven rather than purely descriptive when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design aims that test clear hypotheses; if descriptive work is necessary, justify its value and how it will lead to hypothesis generation or translational steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Aims should be independent so that failure of one aim does not doom the entire project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure aims so each can succeed on its own; avoid aim dependencies that create single points of failure across the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative preliminary data
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide quantitative preliminary data to support feasibility and effect sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include solid preliminary results that demonstrate feasibility and inform power/sample-size calculations; prioritize quantitative evidence where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit rigor and reproducibility language
rubrics_metrics.description: Make explicit statements about rigor and reproducibility practices in the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss study design elements (randomization, blinding, replicates), data management, statistical plans, authentication of resources, and how reproducibility will be ensured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic budgeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a realistic budget that matches project aims and timelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure budget items are justified, consistent with scope, and compliant with funder rules. ORS commonly catches budget errors during pre-submission checks—address they early and consult ORS for complex items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance and regulatory readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Address compliance requirements (e.g., IRB/IACUC, clinical trial registration, COI) within the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and document required approvals and compliance plans; resolve gaps before submission to avoid administrative holds or delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of support specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of support should be specific about commitments and roles rather than generic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain letters that detail what resources, personnel, or access are being committed, including scope, duration, and percent effort where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget errors (pre-submission failure mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common pre-submission problem: budget errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORS screens for inconsistent math, missing budget justification, incorrect fringe/indirect calculations, and noncompliant cost items—correct these before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance gaps (pre-submission failure mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common pre-submission problem: missing or incomplete compliance documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify human subjects, animal, biosafety, export control, and other compliance needs early and include documentation or plans in the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subaward complications (pre-submission failure mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common pre-submission problem: subaward issues/complications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resolve subrecipient commitment forms, budgets, and flow-down clauses in advance; allow time for institutional approvals and negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format violations (pre-submission failure mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common pre-submission problem: format violations (font, page limits, section order, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow sponsor formatting rules exactly (page limits, fonts, margins, required headings). ORS checks for format compliance prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing required sections (pre-submission failure mode)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common pre-submission problem: omitted required sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sponsor checklists to ensure required attachments and sections (e.g., human subjects sections, data management plans, resource sharing plans) are included.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH-specific conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow standard NIH conventions (Specific Aims structure, significance/innovation/approach headings), connect to institute mission, and leverage DCRI/DTMI translational framing for clinical projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to NIH page formats and review criteria language; explicitly state relevance to the target institute's priorities and emphasize translational resources when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF expectations (Pratt/engineering context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize intellectual merit and broader impacts; engineering proposals may highlight industry partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For NSF proposals, explicitly address intellectual merit and broader impacts, and when from Pratt, highlight engineering novelty and potential industry collaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: DARPA / DoD funding themes
rubrics_metrics.description: DARPA/DoD proposals (especially in engineering) should emphasize application areas like AI/ML, materials, and include potential industry partnerships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame proposals to show technological readiness, novel approaches, and possible transition pathways to defense/industry adoption where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation proposals: strategic alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Foundation proposals should align strategically with funder priorities and coordinate with the Office of Foundation Relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work with the Office of Foundation Relations to ensure alignment, tailor narrative to foundation priorities, and provide evidence of strategic fit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary and cross-school collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-school collaborations are encouraged; show interdisciplinary integration and cite cross-cutting institutes (e.g., Duke Forge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document roles, contributions, and institutional support across schools/units to demonstrate true interdisciplinary capacity and added value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation science when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, incorporate implementation science methods to demonstrate how interventions will be adopted in practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe frameworks, outcomes, and measures for implementation and how the project advances adoption, scalability, or health system integration.
